title: fix(app-shell): Setup › Packages draws Actions only over rows that carry one; sheet values wrap at words
body:
Fixes #13166
Clause-②: no

Setup › Packages: the Actions column now shows only when a row in view carries an action, and the package sheet wraps its values at words instead of between any two letters. Both changes are in `PackagesPage.tsx` (`@object-ui/app-shell`), with one new test file and one patch changeset. Why `Clause-②: no`: this changes how the Packages page renders inside `@object-ui/app-shell`. No export, prop or accept set moves.

## What the card measured, and what this changes

The card's reading on HotCRM (objectstack-ai/hotcrm#2188, track 2, F-26): *the Actions header sits over an empty cell in every row (2 app rows, 23 platform rows); in the sheet, the Description breaks inside words ("marketplac / e", "Con / tracts").*

### 1. The empty Actions column

**Mechanism (H1, measured against `origin/main` `05e3f34`).** Two different facts decided the header and the cells:

- the header was drawn whenever `showMarketplaceActions` held, which is page-level: `features.installLocal` on, and the viewer a workspace admin;
- a cell had content only for a row with `source === 'marketplace'` and an install entry from the marketplace list.

So on an install with no marketplace rows, which is the card's case (HotCRM's two `code` packages plus platform packages), every cell under the header was empty. No other row can carry an action in this column. `install` is set only on marketplace rows, and `MarketplaceRowActions` always draws at least Details for an entry it is given.

**Fix.** One helper, `rowActionEntry(row)`, answers "what does this row's Actions cell act on". The cell uses it. The header is `showMarketplaceActions && filtered.some((r) => rowActionEntry(r) !== null)`. Because the header and the cells read the same answer, they can no longer disagree.

**Decision: "in view" means the filtered rows, not all rows.** I chose this over the brief's lean towards the flicker criterion, and checked that criterion myself:

- *Does it flicker?* Search filtering is a substring match, so typing more characters can only remove rows. While typing, the column can disappear at most once, at the moment the last marketplace row leaves. While deleting, it can come back at most once. A `?source=` change or the platform switch is a single discrete step. During a reload the table is replaced by the skeleton, so no frame shows a header without its cells. The column never toggles back and forth; it moves when its cells do.
- *The all-rows alternative.* If the header read all rows, it would never move while filtering. But in any filtered view that hides every marketplace row (`?source=code`, `?source=authored`, or a search), it would draw the card's defect again: a header over all-empty cells.

**Four axes (the brief's framework).**

| | A: rows in view (chosen) | B: all rows | C: copy the sheet's lifecycle actions into the row |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Real business need | Fixes the card's install, and any filtered view. A not-loaded marketplace install has no sheet (no registry row, so the row is not clickable), and its Actions cell is its only door. A keeps that cell exactly where it is needed. | Fixes only the unfiltered view. A filtered view brings back the empty column. | No measured reader needs them. The card's reader found them in the sheet. It would widen the table and draw the same actions twice. |
| Long-term soundness | Header and cells read one helper, so they agree by construction. | Header and cells read different row sets, so a narrower disagreement remains. | A second copy of every lifecycle action, to keep in step with the sheet. |
| Keeps AI from writing it wrong | Layout only, no metadata surface. The next row action added to the cell has to go through the helper the header reads. | Same, but with a second row set to keep in mind. | More surface to drift. |
| No sprawl while we are a startup | No new surface, no new gate. | No new surface, no new gate. | New surface. Rejected. |

### 2. Words broken mid-word in the sheet

**Mechanism (H3, measured in Chromium).** `DetailRow`'s value span was `break-all`, which lets the browser break between any two letters. The `DetailRow` values are Version, Type, Scope (a badge), Status (a badge) and Description. Two of them can carry a long unbroken token: Version (a prerelease or build version) and Description (prose that may contain a URL). The package id is not a `DetailRow`: it is the sheet header's `SheetDescription` line, and this PR does not change it (see Acceptance notes).

**Fix.** The value span is now `min-w-0 break-words`. It breaks at word boundaries first, and inside a token only when that token alone is wider than the line. `min-w-0` lets the flex item shrink below such a token, so the token wraps instead of overflowing. I chose `break-words` because the rest of `app-shell` uses it. `wrap-anywhere` / `[overflow-wrap:anywhere]` has no uses here, and I did not measure it.

## Browser reading (Chromium `/opt/pw-browsers/chromium`, 1440×900)

The real `PackagesPage` rendered against the console's own Tailwind build: an untracked probe entry under `apps/console`, served by my own Vite on a free port, with `fetch` stubbed. The probe files are removed and nothing of them is committed. Fixtures: the card's install, i.e. HotCRM's two `code` packages with HotCRM's own package description, *"AI-Native CRM for the ObjectStack marketplace — Accounts, Contacts, Leads, Opportunities, Cases, Knowledge, Forecasts, Campaigns, Contracts."*, read from objectstack-ai/hotcrm at the evidence commit `ed4f40e42`.

| reading | before (`05e3f34`) | after (`eb799b1c4`, same `PackagesPage.tsx` as the head) |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| list, card's install: headers | Name, ID, Version, Scope, Status, Source, **Actions** | Name, ID, Version, Scope, Status, Source |
| list, card's install: cells per row | 7, the last one empty in both rows | 6 |
| list, plus one marketplace row with an install entry (control) | Actions header; the marketplace row draws Details and Uninstall; the code rows' cells are empty | **unchanged** |
| sheet, Description: "marketplace" | SPLIT across 2 lines | whole |
| sheet, Description: "Contracts" | SPLIT across 2 lines | whole |
| sheet, Description: "Opportunities" | whole | whole |
| sheet, 77-character version token and a URL in the Description, short id (control) | n/a | both wrap inside the value (`right` edge 1416 px = the sheet's content edge); sheet `scrollWidth` 447 = `clientWidth` 447 |

Measured by a `Range` over each word's characters: one line box means whole, more than one means split.

## Tests

`PackagesPage.actionsColumn-13166.test.tsx` has 7 tests:

- no Actions header when no row can hold an action, with the platform rows hidden and shown, and every row has as many cells as the header has columns;
- no header for a marketplace row that the marketplace list does not hold;
- **CONTROL:** with a marketplace row that has an install entry, the header and Details / Uninstall render, the code row's Actions cell is empty, and a row click still opens the sheet;
- "in view" is the filtered rows: a search that hides the marketplace row hides the column and clearing the search restores it; `?source=code` hides it;
- a viewer who is not an admin sees no header;
- the wrap class pin: the Description and Version values carry `break-words` and `min-w-0`, and not `break-all`. Line breaks are a layout fact happy-dom cannot measure, so the browser reading above is that half.

**Ablation.** The fix was committed first. Each mutation went through `ablation-replace.mjs` in wrap mode, which mutates, runs the file, then restores and proves the restore (blob equals `HEAD`, `git diff HEAD` empty):

- the header gate reverted to `const showActionsColumn = showMarketplaceActions;` gives **4 failed | 3 passed**. Red: the two no-header tests, the search test and `?source=code`. Green: the CONTROL test, the non-admin test (`showMarketplaceActions` is already false there) and the wrap pin;
- `DetailRow` reverted to `text-sm font-medium text-right break-all` gives **1 failed | 6 passed** (the wrap pin).

## Local gates (at head `6423fe31d`)

- `pnpm --filter @object-ui/app-shell type-check` exits 0, after building the dependency closure with `turbo run build --filter='@object-ui/app-shell^...'`. `tsconfig.test.json` includes `src/**/*.test.tsx`, so the new test file is compiled.
- `pnpm --filter @object-ui/app-shell lint` exits 0: 0 errors, and no warning on the new test file.
- All 22 test files that name `PackagesPage` exit 0: `Test Files 22 passed (22)`, `Tests 313 passed (313)`.
- `product-neutral-renderer.ratchet.test.ts`: 32 passed.
- `check:new-line-citations` (0 new), `check:control-bytes`, `check:changeset-claims`, `check:pending-changeset-literals`, `check:vi-mock-specifiers`, `check:vi-mock-inherit`, `check:vi-mock-override-shape`, `check:test-path-roots`, `check-changeset-presence.mjs` and `check-changeset-no-major.mjs`: each exits 0.
- Not run, because no user-facing string moved: `check:i18n-keys`, `check:i18n-drift`.
- The full suite and the rest of the farm run in CI.

## Acceptance notes

- **The sheet header's id line has no wrap rule.** This was measured, is unchanged by this PR, and nothing is filed. `SheetDescription` (`font-mono text-xs`) holds the package id. A 96-character id with no hyphen overflows it at both base and head: `scrollWidth` 674 against `clientWidth` 399, and the sheet scrolls sideways (698 against 447). The longest real package id I found in objectstack's own sources is 57 characters (`com.objectstack.cloud-connection.marketplace-installed-ui`). It wraps at its hyphens and fits (399 against 399). The spec's id pattern has no length cap. No real producer reaches the overflow, so it is recorded here and not filed. Owner: none. The brief's H4 control "a long ID still wraps inside the sheet" therefore holds for `DetailRow` values, not for this line.
- **The same class shape exists elsewhere, read but not measured.** In `JobPreview.tsx`, the value span of `ScheduleLine` is `break-all`. Its values are schedule tokens such as cron expressions and time zones, where breaking inside a token may be intended. No browser reading was taken. Owner: none.
